messages.subject: Estimating Animal Population Parameters
parts:
Hi all,
I am a graduate student in the southeastern United States and i am trying to estimate wild animal populations on species that are not individually identifiable. In a survey I conducted, I used remotely triggered cameras (trail-cameras) to collect my data, but i am having difficulty in implementing a model that would give me some indicator of population size (e.g. density, abundance, estimated size). Additionally, I am trying to determine habitat preference as an equal number of cameras were placed in two distinct habitats. 
Context of Survey:
My survey consisted of 20 trail-cameras that were employed in two transects in two distinctive habitats (upland and wetland). Each transect consisted of 10 cameras spaced 0.04 km between each other. The duration of this study lasted 90 days. The data collected included the camera location at which the species was photographed, time at which taken, and date taken. 

Are there any models that could be applied to this survey that would give me some indicator of population size?

Regards and Thank you

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Estimating Animal Population Parameters
parts:
Patrick

Because you have written to the distance sampling email list, you won't be surprised to learn that it may be possible to use distance sampling methods to estimate abundance from the data you have collected.  Recently, distance sampling methods have been described by Howe et al. (2018) for camera traps.  However, as the name implies, this assumes you have the ability to measure the distances from camera to objects in your photos.  In addition, because there tends to be multiple detections of the same animal depending upon the triggering mechanism and recycling time of the camera, over-dispersion can be of concern in the analyses of such data.  Methods to address over-dispersion are described in Howe et al. (2019).

References:

Howe, Eric J., Stephen T. Buckland, Marie-Lyne Després-Einspenner, and Hjalmar S. Kühl. 2018. Distance sampling with camera traps. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, May, 1558–65. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-21...@10.1111/(ISSN)2041-210x.PracticalToolsFieldMethodsMEE32018.
Howe, Eric J., Stephen T. Buckland, Marie-Lyne Després‐Einspenner, and Hjalmar S. Kühl. 2019. Model selection with overdispersed distance sampling data’. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 10 (1): 38–47. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13082.
